introduction.text: Centrale Montemartini is part of the Capitoline Museums, housed in a former municipal power station on Via Ostiense in Rome. The plant opened in 1912, and its restored machine and boiler halls now hold ancient sculptures alongside the industrial equipment preserved inside the building. Two enormous diesel engines form the backdrop to Roman figures in the machine hall. Elsewhere, the collections include Republican portraits, imperial sarcophagi and objects from the burial of Crepereia Tryphaena. Most of the antiquities come from excavations carried out in the second half of the nineteenth century and in the 1930s. The former boiler room 2 also houses carriages from Pope Pius IX's train, while outside stand two elaborate cast-iron lamp posts by Duilio Cambellotti.

history.description: Opened in 1912, the plant was the first to produce electricity for Rome's municipal electricity company. It was named after Giovanni Montemartini, an advocate of bringing public services under municipal control.
In 1997, antiquities displaced by renovations at the Capitoline Museums went on display here in the exhibition Machines and Gods. What began as a temporary arrangement became a permanent museum.

design.description: The plant was built near the Tiber for a steady supply of water, with road and railway connections nearby. It stood outside the city's customs boundary, where fuel was exempt from import duties.
The plant combined steam turbines with diesel engines. The turbines supplied continuous power, while the engines were brought into use when electricity demand was highest.
Two elaborate cast-iron lamp posts designed by Duilio Cambellotti stand outside the building.

art.description: In the machine hall, ancient sculptures stand in front of two enormous diesel engines. The display keeps the industrial machinery visible alongside the antiquities.
The collections include Roman portraits and imperial sarcophagi. The sarcophagus of Crepereia Tryphaena is displayed with objects from her burial.
The former boiler room 2 houses carriages from Pope Pius IX's train, another part of the museum's collection beyond the ancient sculpture.
